title: Rigveda 5.51: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 5.51: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 5.51 is a hymn of 15 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 5, the family book of the Atri clan. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 368r-369r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 5.51.1-4 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 368r
translation.original_text:
1agne̍ su̱tasya̍ pī̱taye̱ viśvai̱r ūme̍bhi̱r ā ga̍hi | de̱vebhi̍r ha̱vyadā̍taye ||
2ṛta̍dhītaya̱ ā ga̍ta̱ satya̍dharmāṇo adhva̱ram | a̱gneḥ pi̍bata ji̱hvayā̍ ||
3vipre̍bhir vipra santya prāta̱ryāva̍bhi̱r ā ga̍hi | de̱vebhi̱ḥ soma̍pītaye ||
4a̱yaṁ soma̍ś ca̱mū su̱to 'ma̍tre̱ pari̍ ṣicyate | pri̱ya indrā̍ya vā̱yave̍ ||
translation.text:
1WITH all assistants, Agni, come hither to drink the Soma-juice; With Gods unto our sacred gifts.
2Come to the sacrifice, O ye whose ways are right, whose laws are true, And drink the draught with Agni's tongue.
3O Singer, with the singers, O Gracious, with those who move at dawn, Come to the Soma-draught with Gods.
4To Indra and to Vâyu dear, this Soma, by the mortar pressed, Is now poured forth to fill the jar.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 368r (numbered 41r by the scribe) (OPenn image 368, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 5.50.4 ‹-arṇāḥ dhīrāiva sanitā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 368v (numbered 41v by the scribe), begins in RV 5.51.5 ‹-sutasya andhasaḥ abhi prayaḥ›. Verses 5.51.1-4 end on this page.

1agne | sutasya | pītaye | viśvaiḥ | ūmebhiḥ | ā | gahi | devebhiḥ | havya-dātaye
2ṛta-dhītayaḥ | ā | gata | satya-dharmāṇaḥ | adhvaram | agneḥ | pibata | jihvayā
3viprebhiḥ | vipra | santya | prātaryāva-bhiḥ | ā | gahi | devebhiḥ | soma-pītaye
4ayam | somaḥ | camū iti | sutaḥ | amatre | pari | sicyate | priyaḥ | indrāya | vāyave

translation.original_ref: RV 5.51.5-10 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 5); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 368v
translation.original_text:
5vāya̱v ā yā̍hi vī̱taye̍ juṣā̱ṇo ha̱vyadā̍taye | pibā̍ su̱tasyāndha̍so a̱bhi praya̍ḥ ||
6indra̍ś ca vāyav eṣāṁ su̱tānā̍m pī̱tim a̍rhathaḥ | tāñ ju̍ṣethām are̱pasā̍v a̱bhi praya̍ḥ ||
7su̱tā indrā̍ya vā̱yave̱ somā̍so̱ dadhyā̍śiraḥ | ni̱mnaṁ na ya̍nti̱ sindha̍vo̱ 'bhi praya̍ḥ ||
8sa̱jūr viśve̍bhir de̱vebhi̍r a̱śvibhyā̍m u̱ṣasā̍ sa̱jūḥ | ā yā̍hy agne atri̱vat su̱te ra̍ṇa ||
9sa̱jūr mi̱trāvaru̍ṇābhyāṁ sa̱jūḥ some̍na̱ viṣṇu̍nā | ā yā̍hy agne atri̱vat su̱te ra̍ṇa ||
10sa̱jūr ā̍di̱tyair vasu̍bhiḥ sa̱jūr indre̍ṇa vā̱yunā̍ | ā yā̍hy agne atri̱vat su̱te ra̍ṇa ||
translation.text:
5Vâyu, come hither to the feast, wellpleased unto our sacred gifts: Drink of the Soma juice effused come to the food.
6Ye, Indra, Vâyu, well deserve to drink the juices pressed by us. Gladly accept them, spotless Pair come to the food.
7For Indra and for Vâyu pressed are Soma juices blent with curd, As rivers to the lowland flow: come to the food.
8Associate with all the Gods, come, with the Aṣvins and with Dawn, Agni, as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.
9Associate with Varuṇa, with Mitra, Soma, Vishṇu, come, Agni, as erstwith Atri, so enjoy the juice.
10Associate with Vasus, with Âdityas, Indra, Viyu, come, Agni as erst with Atri, so enjoy the juice.

translation.original_ref: RV 5.51.11-15 (aṣṭaka 4, adhyāya 3, varga 7); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 369r
translation.original_text:
11sva̱sti no̍ mimītām a̱śvinā̱ bhaga̍ḥ sva̱sti de̱vy adi̍tir ana̱rvaṇa̍ḥ | sva̱sti pū̱ṣā asu̍ro dadhātu naḥ sva̱sti dyāvā̍pṛthi̱vī su̍ce̱tunā̍ ||
12sva̱staye̍ vā̱yum upa̍ bravāmahai̱ soma̍ṁ sva̱sti bhuva̍nasya̱ yas pati̍ḥ | bṛha̱spati̱ṁ sarva̍gaṇaṁ sva̱staye̍ sva̱staya̍ ādi̱tyāso̍ bhavantu naḥ ||
13viśve̍ de̱vā no̍ a̱dyā sva̱staye̍ vaiśvāna̱ro vasu̍r a̱gniḥ sva̱staye̍ | de̱vā a̍vantv ṛ̱bhava̍ḥ sva̱staye̍ sva̱sti no̍ ru̱draḥ pā̱tv aṁha̍saḥ ||
14sva̱sti mi̍trāvaruṇā sva̱sti pa̍thye revati | sva̱sti na̱ indra̍ś cā̱gniś ca̍ sva̱sti no̍ adite kṛdhi ||
15sva̱sti panthā̱m anu̍ carema sūryācandra̱masā̍v iva | puna̱r dada̱tāghna̍tā jāna̱tā saṁ ga̍memahi ||
translation.text:
11May Bhaga and the Aṣvins grant us health and wealth, and Goddess Adid and he whom none resist. The Asura Pûshan grant us all prosperity, and Heaven and Earth most wise vouchsafe us happiness.
12Let us solicit Vâyu for prosperity, and Soma who is Lord of all the world for weal; For weal Br̥ihaspati with all his company. May the Âdityas bring us health and happiness.
13May all the Gods, may Agni the beneficent, God of all men, this day be with us for our weal. Help us the R̥ibhus, the Divine Ones, for our good. May Rudra bless and keep us from calamity.
14Prosper us, Mitra, Varuṇa. O wealthy Pathyâ, prosper us. Indra and Agni, prosper us; prosper us thou, O Aditi.
15Like Sun and Moon may we pursue in full prosperity our path, And meet with one who gives again, -who knows us well and slays us not.
